examples.text: His laden feet sand and stuck in mire; he was bedaubed with the blue-gray clay from head to foot; but he had escaped the deadly river!

glosses: A bog or fen; (in wetland science, specifically) a peatland which is actively forming peat, such as an active bog or fen.

examples.text: Glagolev […] measured CH₄ emission from a mire in West Siberia using a static chamber method. Similar methods had been developed and tested by Nakano et al. (2006), Fig. 1.

Swansea seemed to be pulling clear of trouble with five wins in their first eight games following head coach Paul Clement's appointment, but two successive defeats had dragged the Swans back into the mire.

glosses: To cause or permit to become stuck in mud; to plunge or fix in mud.

examples.text: to mire a horse or wagon

glosses: To soil with mud or foul matter.

examples.text:
Why had I not with charitable hand
Took up a beggar’s issue at my gates,
Who smirch’d thus and mired with infamy,
I might have said ‘No part of it is mine;
This shame derives itself from unknown loins’?
